findings.title: Unused logging import and module logger left behind by refactor
findings.body: After the extracted logic moved into incidents.py, `import logging` on line 4 and `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` on line 11 are dead code in mark_failed.py — the module no longer emits any log statements. A refactor that removes the only consumers of this logger is the natural place to clean it up; leaving it in is misleading and will trip unused-import linters.

findings.title: Unused logger definition in the new module
findings.body: `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` on line 25 is defined but never referenced anywhere in the new incident_occurrence.py (the imports of `logging` on line 3 exist solely to support this dead definition). It should be removed together with the now-unused `import logging` so the new module is consistent with mark_failed.py's behavior.

findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context modifies a config copy it never returns
findings.body: In `get_monitor_environment_context`, `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` on line 160 and `config['schedule_type'] = monitor_environment.monitor.get_schedule_type_display()` on line 162 are dead code: the dict returned on line 168 uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original) instead of the modified local `config`. Consequence: the `monitor.config` payload sent in issue events via Kafka always contains the raw `schedule_type` enum value and never the human-readable display string the code clearly intended to substitute. The bug is preserved verbatim from the pre-refactor mark_failed.py, but hoisting the function into its own module is the right place to fix it — either return `config` or drop the unused local.
